reason: The cited evidence supports that actively learned MTPs achieve DFT accuracy for energies and forces in multicomponent alloys (E1, E3) and that vibrational entropy can be extracted from AIMD displacement covariances (E4), but no evidence is provided for ML potentials capturing electron–vibration coupling, achieving the claimed speed-up with 10% free-energy fidelity, or outperforming TOR-TILD in compositional scaling.
premises: ML potentials can be trained to DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys using active learning
ML potentials can capture vibrational entropy and anharmonicity via training on AIMD trajectories and displacement covariances
ML potentials can incorporate electron–vibration coupling effects
ML-driven free-energy calculations are significantly faster than explicit AIMD while retaining ~10% accuracy
ML potentials scale better than TOR-TILD for compositional exploration
